extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry (readers familiar with or studying Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmüller theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and conceptual checks for formulating, interpreting, and evaluating constructions/identifications in inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT), especially concerning RCS assertions, Θ- and log-links, coricity/symmetry properties, and the treatment of arithmetic fundamental groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCS-redundancy assertions (RC-FrÉt), (RC-log), (RC-Θ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertions by adherents of the RCS that implementing the RCS-identifications (RC-log), (RC-Θ) makes Frobenius-like/étale-like distinctions trivial, summarized symbolically as (RC-log), (RC-Θ) ⇒ (RC-FrÉt) and (RC-FrÉt),(RC-log),(RC-Θ) ⇒ (1-Dim).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper argues these assertions are at best misleading: the RCS-identifications do not resolve relationships between corresponding objects in distinct (Θ±ellNF-)Hodge theaters but instead translate those issues into tracking effects along composites of Θ- and log-links. Treat claims of RCS-redundancy with caution and check whether purported 'trivializations' actually hide nontrivial path-tracking along links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid assuming a single fixed ring/scheme category (FxRng)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many arithmetic geometers' intuition comes from working where all schemes/rings belong to a single category fixed throughout the theory, leading to assertions of RCS-redundancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not tacitly assume that all rings/schemes in a theory are related by ring homomorphisms respecting ring structure. If constructions rely on such fixed-category intuition, explicitly verify whether the required homomorphisms or identifications exist; failure of that assumption can invalidate RCS-style identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy-awareness: historical precedents (FxEuc, FxFld, RdVar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize historical analogies (e.g., abstract manifolds vs ambient Euclidean space, use of Galois groups/abstract fields, non-reduced schemes) when evaluating receptivity to novel abstract structures in IUT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these analogies to understand possible resistance to IUT ideas. However, do not conflate historical acceptability with mathematical validity; check the specific structural roles (e.g., nilpotents, abstract groups) in the present theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat arithmetic fundamental groups as abstract topological groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Étale-like objects correspond for the most part to arithmetic fundamental groups (π1(X) etc.) and 'it is of fundamental importance that these arithmetic fundamental groups be treated simply as abstract topological groups.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reconstructing objects from fundamental groups or comparing objects across Hodge theaters, work with the groups as abstract topological objects (without rigidifying them as Galois groups acting on fixed fields). Many coricity/symmetry properties and multiradial reconstruction algorithms depend on this abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coricity and permutation symmetry for étale-like objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Étale-like objects satisfy horizontal/vertical coricity properties mapping isomorphically to neighboring Hodge theaters and a crucial symmetry property with respect to permutation of adjacent vertical lines of the log-theta-lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify coricity/symmetry when claiming that an object reconstructs identically across neighboring theaters. These properties are formal consequences of treating fundamental groups abstractly and are central to multiradial algorithms; Frobenius-like objects typically do not satisfy them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume Frobenius-like objects inherit coricity/symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Frobenius-like objects depend on the coordinates (n,m) of a Hodge theater and, unlike étale-like objects, do not satisfy the coricity/symmetry properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When moving between theaters or applying identifications like (RC-log) or (RC-Θ), explicitly check whether an object is Frobenius-like or étale-like; do not presume coricity for Frobenius-like objects, and be skeptical of any argument that pretends RCS-identifications force such coricity.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCS-identifications translate, not resolve, theater-comparison issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing RCS-identifications makes there 'only one' Hodge theater superficially, but this merely translates the issue of relating objects at distinct coordinates into tracking the effect along composites of Θ- and log-links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether purported simplifications via RCS actually reduce complexity or merely relocate it to the analysis of link-composites; require explicit control of how objects transform under Θ- and log-links rather than relying on an identification shortcut.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret 'identity isomorphisms' only at weaker underlying structures
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'identity isomorphism' can be misleading because it is only well-defined as an isomorphism from an object to itself; in contexts of Θk or logk one must apply it to weaker structures (sets, abstract topological groups/monoids) that genuinely coincide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using 'identity isomorphism' to mean an isomorphism between distinct objects with different ring structures. Instead, specify the weaker structure (e.g., as abstract topological group or monoid) in which the identity identification is being made, to prevent confusion and invalid conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain coric structures via indeterminate isomorphisms (i-e)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain coric structures that are invariant and well-defined independent of domain/codomain specifications, one must regard isomorphisms Gk ∼→ Gk and Π ∼→ Π as indeterminate isomorphisms of abstract groups, and the 'identity isomorphism' on O×μk as an indeterminate isomorphism of topological monoids with extra submonoid data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When formulating coricity, work with indeterminate/abstract isomorphism classes rather than specific Galois-rigidified realizations. Check invariance against the required collection of submonoids and actions by open subgroups, as described in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with ring structures: Θk and logk failures (i-a, i-b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The isomorphism Θk : FN ∼→ F1 and the map logk : O×k → k are not compatible with the ring structures in their domain/codomain; they do not arise from Gk-equivariant ring homomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume existence of underlying ring homomorphisms inducing Θk or logk. Verify consequences at the level of value groups and divisibility properties of units; failures of ring-compatibility are central to several non-symmetry and non-commutativity phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivariance/compatibility at group/monoid level (i-c, i-d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although not ring-compatible, Θk and logk are compatible in the sense of equivariance with respect to the natural actions (Θk with Gk, logk with Π).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compatibility is needed, phrase it at the level of topological group/monoid equivariance rather than ring homomorphisms. The correct notion of compatibility for many reconstructions is equivariance of actions, not ring morphism compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry failure under switching domain/codomain (ii-a, ii-b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Θk and logk are not symmetric with respect to switching domain/codomain: there do not exist Gk-equivariant ring homomorphisms making the natural diagrams commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When checking bidirectional symmetry, trace elements at the level of value groups (e.g., images of qN or certain units) to detect asymmetry. Do not assume diagrams commute merely because topological/group-level diagrams appear symmetric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry can hold at abstract group action level if coricity applied (ii-c)
rubrics_metrics.description: A manifest symmetry arises for topological group actions surrounding Θk when the coricity properties (i-e, i-f) are applied, i.e., when isomorphisms are regarded as indeterminate isomorphisms of abstract topological groups/monoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish symmetry as a property of abstract equivariant group/monoid diagrams from symmetry at the level of ring-structured diagrams. Apply coricity hypotheses if one wishes to use symmetry in arguments; otherwise symmetry may fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-commutativity/non-invariance of Θk and logk (iii-a, iii-b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Θk does not commute with logk and Θk is not invariant with respect to logk in the sense that no pair of Gk-equivariant ring homomorphisms can be found to make the corresponding composites/diagrams commute on their domains of definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly test commutativity by attempting to construct the required Gk-equivariant ring maps and tracing specific elements (e.g., images of exp(pn·N) or elements in given value ranges). Avoid arguments that tacitly assume Θ and log commute or that Θ is invariant under log.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and role of global multiplicative subspace (GMS) and global canonical generator (GCG)
rubrics_metrics.description: A GMS M ⊆ E[l] and a GCG γ ∈ (E[l]/M)(F) (if they exist) equip E[l] with a canonical multiplicative subspace and canonical generator (up to ±1); existence implies relations like qE* = qE^l at nonarchimedean primes of bad multiplicative reduction and yields height bounds for E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using isogeny/height arguments (as in Example 3.2.1), verify whether a global multiplicative subspace and canonical generator exist. If absent, the standard argument breaks down; in IUT one must 'simulate' a GMS/GCG via theta functions and mono-anabelian techniques to recover analogous bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulate GMS/GCG and use theta + mono-anabelian geometry to bound heights
rubrics_metrics.description: To generalize invariance-of-height arguments to elliptic curves that do not admit a GMS, one must somehow 'simulate' a GMS/GCG and apply the theory of theta functions and mono-anabelian geometry (the Θ-pilot, log-Kummer-correspondence, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In proofs aiming to obtain height bounds without genuine GMS/GCG, ensure the simulation mechanism is made explicit (how the Θ-pilot supplies a multiradial container for Frobenius-like data) and verify that the theta/mono-anabelian machinery indeed provides the needed structural replacements.
